item.title: Python NodeStealer Evolves Into AI-Assisted Spyware With Telegram C2
item.content:encoded:
Window: 02 Sep 18:00 → 02 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Python NodeStealer: AI-Assisted to Full Spyware — Should Read

Netskope researchers report that Python NodeStealer has evolved from a Facebook/browser infostealer into full spyware with keylogging, clipboard monitoring, screenshots, Wi-Fi and picture theft, and expanded Facebook Graph API harvesting. The new variant also uses split Telegram C2 channels and shows signs that its added capabilities were AI-assisted.

  • Netskope Threat Labs found an August 2026 Python NodeStealer variant with full spyware capabilities, including keystroke logging, clipboard monitoring, screenshot capture, and a dual Telegram bot command-and-control architecture.
  • The latest NodeStealer variant expands its theft targets to include Wi-Fi passwords, the victim’s Pictures folder, and two additional web browsers.
  • The new variant queries more than 20 Facebook Graph API endpoints covering identity, social graph, account security, advertising, and commerce data, compared with two endpoints in earlier variants.
  • Netskope Threat Labs observed indicators that newly added NodeStealer functions may have been AI-assisted, including systematic use of decorative emojis in output logs that was absent from previous variants.
  • The campaign’s victims were mainly in Asia and North America across multiple segments, with the financial services sector most represented.

item.title: CVE-2026-81891 elFinder ZIP Extraction MIME Bypass Enables Remote Code Execution
item.content:encoded:
Window: 02 Sep 14:00 → 02 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-81891) elFinder Remote Code Execution via ZIP Extraction MIME Bypass — Should Read

CVE-2026-81891 is a high-severity elFinder flaw that can let attackers achieve remote code execution by uploading and extracting ZIP archives containing PHP-executable files that bypass MIME checks. Organizations should upgrade to elFinder 2.1.70, restrict connector access, and block PHP execution in upload/extraction directories.

  • CVE-2026-81891 is an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in Studio 42 elFinder that can allow remote code execution through archive extraction.
  • The flaw occurs because checkExtractItems() calls mimetypeInternalDetect() without normalizing the detected MIME type, allowing PHP-executable extensions such as .phtml, .phar, .php5, and .php3 to bypass the uploadDeny filter.
  • All elFinder releases prior to 2.1.70 are affected, and version 2.1.70 fixes the MIME validation gap during archive extraction.
  • Affected assets are typically PHP web applications that embed elFinder as a file browser or media manager, often inside CMSs, admin panels, e-commerce back offices, customer portals, and internal file-sharing tools.
  • Recommended actions include inventorying elFinder deployments, restricting connector access, disabling archive extraction where unnecessary, blocking PHP execution in upload and extraction directories, and monitoring for unexpected PHP-executable files or requests.

Technologies: cms, web-server

Products: elfinder, cycognito-platform

Vendors: studio-42, cycognito

item.title: Gambling Goblin SEO abuse, DKIM-signed Reply-To diversion, and AI medical device pentesting
item.content:encoded:

Gaming the system: how a Chinese-speaking actor turned Brazilian government sites into an SEO weapon — Must Read

Check Point Research says a Chinese-speaking cybercrime group linked to Earth Berberoka is compromising Brazilian government and education web servers, installing malicious Apache modules that turn trusted domains into stealth proxies for gambling-themed fake app-store pages and SEO manipulation. The same scalable infrastructure and Linux malware toolkit could be quickly repurposed from search fraud to direct malware delivery.

  • Check Point Research tracked a sustained campaign since mid-2025 against Brazilian organizations, primarily government and educational institutions, by a Chinese-speaking cybercrime cluster it calls Gambling Goblin.
  • The attackers install malicious Apache modules on compromised web servers to reverse-proxy selected visitors to attacker-controlled phishing pages while the traffic appears to come from the legitimate domain.
  • The phishing pages impersonate trusted app-distribution platforms such as Google Play, Microsoft Store, and Amazon while promoting online gambling and sports betting to Brazilian users.
  • The group deploys a heavily obfuscated Linux toolkit that includes DownPro, AlphaAgent, oRAT, a 3snake-based credential stealer, an SSH brute-forcer, and reconnaissance tools.
  • Check Point Research found related phishing networks localized in Vietnamese, Spanish, and English, as well as infrastructure that generates fresh domains daily.

Technologies: web-server, proxy, remote-access, cloud-platform

Products: apache-http-server, google-play, microsoft-store, amazon-appstore, bing, grpc

Vendors: apache-software-foundation, google, microsoft, amazon, cloudflare

Fully Signed, Fully Passed: The Reply-To Was the Payload — Should Read

A genuine European government mailbox sent a fully authenticated phishing email whose only payload was a hidden Reply-To diversion to an attacker-controlled address. Because DKIM, DMARC, and ARC all passed, the key lesson is that email authentication proves origin and integrity, not whether the reply path is safe.

  • A senior executive at a professional certification and credentialing organization received a one-line RFQ follow-up email from a genuine mailbox at a European regional government body.
  • The message had no link or attachment and used a Reply-To field containing both an attacker-controlled address, infodesk@frontdesk-investment[.]com, and the genuine government mailbox.
  • The government domain’s valid DKIM signature explicitly covered the Reply-To header, showing the covert reply address was present before the sending organization’s outbound gateway signed the message.
  • The email passed DKIM twice, DMARC, ARC, and Microsoft’s composite authentication verdict, demonstrating that the message was not forged even though its reply path was redirected.
  • The article says the practical control is to surface reply-path divergence during triage, especially when an inbound message’s reply domain does not match the From domain or contains multiple reply addresses.

UK Cybercrime Journal: ExfilSquad Emerges — Must Read

ExfilSquad is targeting UK public sector, education, and law enforcement organizations with data-theft-only extortion, exploiting exposed SaaS, CRM, and Microsoft Power Pages configurations rather than deploying ransomware. The key risk is that misconfigured cloud-facing business portals can leak large volumes of sensitive contact and administrative data, which the group then distributes via torrents to increase pressure on victims.

  • In mid-2026, the cybercriminal group ExfilSquad launched an extortion campaign targeting prominent UK organizations across the public sector, education, and law enforcement, as well as other firms worldwide.
  • ExfilSquad operates as a pure data extortion group that steals data and threatens to publish it on its onion-based Data Leak Site if a ransom is not paid, rather than deploying encryptors or destructive malware.
  • The UK Department for Education, the Police National Legal Database, and Newcastle University confirmed breaches linked to ExfilSquad involving hundreds of thousands of records and, in the PNLD case, data affecting over 100,000 police officers, staff, and criminal justice professionals.
  • Analysis of ExfilSquad’s leak site details indicated that its primary attack vector involves exploiting misconfigurations in cloud portals, CRM platforms, internal case management systems, and publicly accessible Microsoft Power Pages data tables.
  • ExfilSquad uploaded multi-gigabyte torrent files for each victim to its TOR leak site and assigned distinct Torrent Trackers and initial Web Seeds per victim.

Technologies: cloud-platform, database

Products: microsoft-power-pages, salesforce, snowflake, salesloft

Vendors: microsoft, salesforce, snowflake, salesloft

Policy on Paper, Risk in Practice — Optional

Most organizations have AI data security policies, but fewer than one in 10 can enforce them consistently in real time across AI tools. The key risk is that sensitive data now moves through prompts, copy-paste, and AI-generated outputs faster than traditional file-based controls can track or block.

  • Nearly half of surveyed organizations still rely on written policies, post-event monitoring, or inconsistently enforced controls as their primary approach to data security enforcement.
  • Only 11% of organizations enforce data protection policies in real time across most environments, and only 8% do so for AI tools specifically.
  • Although 67% of organizations maintain a formal AI policy, fewer than one in 10 enforce it consistently in AI environments.
  • Most data protection architectures were built for files, while sensitive information increasingly moves through prompts, AI-generated summaries, and copy-pasted excerpts.
  • Only one in five organizations can apply consistent policy to prompt and text submissions into AI tools, and fewer than one in ten can recognize sensitive data once it has been modified, reformatted, or partially copied.

item.title: CVE-2026-6471 Enables PostgreSQL Replication Accounts to Execute Arbitrary Code
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Sep 22:00 → 02 Sep 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

PostGREShell: The database powering much of the internet had an open door for 12 years — Must Read

Cyera researchers found a critical PostgreSQL flaw, CVE-2026-6471, that lets low-privilege replication accounts load arbitrary plugins and gain remote code execution, superuser access, and persistence. Organizations should patch immediately, audit replication accounts, and restrict replication access and outbound SMB/NFS traffic.

  • Cyera Research discovered CVE-2026-6471, a critical PostgreSQL vulnerability affecting every PostgreSQL version from 9.4 through 18.
  • The flaw lets an account with the REPLICATION attribute load and execute arbitrary code through the logical replication output plugin path because the plugin name is passed to the loader without validation.
  • On Windows, an attacker can exploit the issue remotely by using a UNC path over SMB so PostgreSQL loads a DLL from the attacker’s server without placing a file on the target system.
  • After code execution, the attacker can escalate to PostgreSQL superuser by calling internal functions and directly modifying pg_authid, bypassing normal SQL permission checks.
  • The article recommends applying the PostgreSQL security update, auditing REPLICATION accounts, restricting replication access in pg_hba.conf, and blocking outbound SMB and NFS from database servers.

Technologies: database

item.title: Healthcare Sharing, UK OT Proof, Snowflake Controls, and Self-Spoofed Phishing
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Sep 10:00 → 01 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

The Email From Yourself That Your Own Domain Disowned — May Read

A phishing email spoofed a financial advisor’s own address and reached the inbox despite SPF, DKIM, and DMARC failures because enforcement and composite authentication did not block it. The lure used a legitimate monday.com tracking link to redirect to a disposable credential-harvesting page, highlighting the need to flag self-addressed spoofing and inspect final link destinations.

  • A client-facing financial advisor received a document-signature phishing email whose From and To headers were both the advisor’s own work address.
  • The email arrived from commodity bulk-hosting infrastructure, explicitly failed SPF, had no DKIM signature, failed DMARC, yet Microsoft composite authentication returned a pass.
  • The “Start signing” button routed through a legitimate monday.com link-tracking hostname whose embedded token decoded to a disposable credential-harvesting page on sharedfile.realestatecotblrp.vu.
  • IRONSCALES Themis scored the message at 90% confidence and labeled it credential theft based on the suspicious link and the sender pattern of an external sender using an internal-looking self-addressed email.
  • The article recommends alerting on inbound mail where the From address matches the receiving mailbox, enforcing DMARC, watching for disagreement between authentication results, and resolving vendor link trackers before trusting them.

Technologies: email-security

Products: monday-com-link-tracker, themis, ironscales-adaptive-ai

Vendors: microsoft, monday-com, ironscales, colocrossing

What the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill’s New Standard of Proof Means for OT Organisations — Optional

The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill would push OT organisations from periodic compliance evidence to continuous, defensible proof that they know their assets, risks, ownership, and changes in real time. Many OT environments lack that live visibility today, so boards should close the gap before regulators or incidents force the issue.

  • The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, as currently drafted, introduces a requirement for organisations to show ongoing proof that they manage cyber risk in their plants rather than relying on reasonable periodic effort.
  • The article says policies, point-in-time audits, named risk owners, and older penetration test reports will not be enough to answer regulator questions about what is connected to the network today, what has changed, or what current risk looks like.
  • OT environments are described as harder to manage continuously than IT environments because they often accumulate equipment over decades, include vendor-installed remote access, and have network changes made to maintain operations without formal records.
  • A defensible response requires a current asset inventory, risk scoring tied to operational function, mapping to a recognised methodology such as IEC 62443’s zone and conduit model, and clear ownership with a defined review cadence.
  • The article argues that many boards have not yet tested the gap between believing OT risk is managed and being able to prove it, and that closing this gap before a regulatory conversation is stronger than doing so during one.

Technologies: ics-scada, plc, network-monitoring, remote-access

item.title: Mirage Kitten Deploys NodeRabbit and PollCat RATs Against MEA Aviation and FinTech
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Sep 06:00 → 01 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Mirage Kitten targeting aviation and FinTech sectors across the Middle East and Africa with a new malware set — Must Read

Kaspersky reports that Mirage Kitten is targeting aviation and fintech organizations in the Middle East and Africa with new cross-platform Node.js/JavaScript RATs called NodeRabbit and PollCat, delivered through fake recruiter coding challenges. The campaign marks a shift in the group’s tooling while continuing its use of LinkedIn lures, cloud-hosted infrastructure, and developer-focused social engineering.

  • Kaspersky uncovered two previously undocumented cross-platform RAT families, NodeRabbit and PollCat, during monitoring of Mirage Kitten activity.
  • Mirage Kitten delivered NodeRabbit and PollCat through spear-phishing messages on LinkedIn and other job search platforms that contained trojanized coding challenge archives.
  • NodeRabbit is built with Node.js, targets Windows, Linux, and macOS, and was observed in variants on systems in Afghanistan, Egypt, and Ethiopia.
  • PollCat is written in obfuscated JavaScript, starts during the fake React coding challenge application startup, and can continue running even if the user fails OTP validation.
  • Kaspersky attributes the activity to Mirage Kitten with high confidence based on malware similarities to Retrograde/MiniFast, victimology, lure-hosting tradecraft, and infrastructure patterns.

item.title: Anubis Hits Fairlife; pnpm 12 Rust Rewrite Adds Supply Chain Controls
item.content:encoded:
Window: 01 Sep 02:00 → 01 Sep 06:00 UTC (4 hours)

From a Stolen Login to a Ransomware Leak Site: What Our Telemetry Shows About the Path Threat Actors Take — Should Read

Constella links Fairlife’s public Anubis ransomware leak to a broader pattern where stolen credentials from infostealer-infected vendor laptops can give attackers access to corporate CMS, cloud, SSO, and internal systems. The key takeaway is that third-party credential exposure, including cookies and browser autofill data, must be monitored as seriously as a company’s own endpoints because it can become the first step toward ransomware.

  • Anubis added Fairlife, a dairy brand owned by The Coca-Cola Company, to its dark web extortion portal, and Coca-Cola publicly confirmed the ransomware incident.
  • Anubis claimed it exfiltrated close to a terabyte of internal data and used an optional wipe mode against part of the victim’s virtualization infrastructure.
  • The leaked data was organized into engineering and OT documentation, production and formulation data, and HR and people data.
  • Constella analyzed a separate credential package believed to belong to a third-party digital agency employee that contained 789 saved credential pairs, 540 browser session cookies, and a local password manager vault store.
  • The credential package included hundreds of credentials for brand site content management environments, plus credentials for cloud infrastructure, DevOps, source control, corporate identity, and SSO providers.

Technologies: cms, cloud-platform

Products: hunter-plus, adobe-experience-manager, crxde-lite, package-manager, amazon-web-services, slack

Vendors: constella, adobe, amazon-web-services, slack

pnpm 12’s Rust Rewrite Cuts Install Times by Up to 90% — May Read

pnpm 12 is now stable with a Rust rewrite that keeps pnpm 11 compatibility while delivering major install-time and storage improvements in early real-world testing. Its maintainers have narrowed public benchmark claims after flawed cross-package-manager comparisons, emphasizing faster pnpm performance rather than claiming overall market leadership.

  • pnpm 12 is now stable and replaces pnpm’s Node.js and TypeScript foundation with a Rust rewrite while preserving the commands, settings, and lockfile format used by pnpm 11.
  • In Vercel’s 21-project Turborepo workspace, pnpm 12 reduced median install times by 64.4% to 90.5% compared with pnpm 10.28 across six tested scenarios.
  • pnpm removed Bun and Yarn from the comparison displayed on its benchmark page after bugs made published cross-tool package manager rankings unreliable.
  • pnpm 12 adds supply chain security-related features including project-aware global bins, direct package manager provisioning, registry revisions, signed remote build artifacts, and deterministic cyclic lockfiles.
  • The upgrade has behavioral changes that may affect workflows, including removal of `pnpm install --resolution-only`, canonical HTTPS resolution for Git dependencies on GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket, and warnings for unknown settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

Technologies: source-control
